title: Clarion Claims brings AI damage capture to Australian motor claims
full_text:
Clarion Claims has partnered with Austin, Texas-based RAVIN AI to embed AI-powered vehicle damage assessment into its motor claims operations, with the integration designed to give brokers, insurers, and fleet operators faster and more objective information from the moment a claim is lodged.
The technology sits inside Curium, the claims and compliance platform that powers Clarion’s end-to-end motor claims service. Drivers and fleet managers can photograph exterior vehicle damage through a standard mobile web browser at the scene of an incident – no app download required. RAVIN AI’s computer-vision system then grades the damage and identifies a likely repair pathway, with results flowing directly into Clarion’s triage, assessment, repair management, and reporting workflows.
Under the current model for many claims, repair pathway decisions cannot begin until after a physical assessor visits the vehicle – a step that can add days to an already stretched process.
Clarion says the integration moves that decision-making to day one. Brokers managing fleet clients or volumes of personal lines motor claims gain real-time dashboard visibility into open claims rather than waiting on manual status updates.
The companies also say that verified damage data captured at intake helps surface subrogation and third-party liability opportunities earlier, before they can be lost as a file progresses through the system.
Clarion co-founder and CEO Drew Schnehage (pictured) said the partnership targets the administrative friction that brokers and policyholders experience most acutely. “Claims management has been weighed down by administrative delay for too long, with brokers and drivers constantly chasing updates. At Clarion we start with the claim experience and work backwards, using technology to take the friction out. RAVIN AI gives policyholders, drivers, and fleet operators an instant, app-free way to capture damage at the scene, which speeds up the whole claims lifecycle from day one,” she said.
Tetiana George, co-founder of Clarion and CEO of Curium, said the platform is built around automation and professional judgment working together. “We built Curium so that experienced claims judgement and automation work together, because that is how you scale claims management without losing quality. Clarion is Curium in the hands of claims professionals. Integrating RAVIN AI’s visual intelligence into the platform gives our clients clarity on vehicle condition at intake, and every decision that follows is tracked, auditable, and compliant,” she said.
Clarion is backed by Correlation Risk Partners and serves insurers, brokers, underwriting agencies, MGAs, and fleet operators. The Curium platform received an Australian and New Zealand Institute of Insurance and Finance (ANZIIF) award for claims and compliance.

The partnership arrives as Australian motor claims handling faces sustained regulatory and complaint pressure – context that shapes the commercial case for what Clarion is offering.
The Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) received 34,231 general insurance complaints in 2024-25, a 17% increase on the prior year. Comprehensive motor vehicle insurance was the most complained-about product. Delay in claim handling ranked among the top three issues across all financial products.
AFCA chief ombudsman David Locke has acknowledged that parts and labour shortages contribute to delays but said communication remains a separate and controllable problem. “A lot of issues there around shortages in both labour and parts are impacting that, but clearly there’s a lack of communication and really helping consumers through that period,” Locke told the Australian Associated Press.
The industry’s own compliance data reinforces the picture. The General Insurance Code Governance Committee (GICGC) recorded 70,325 code breaches in 2024-25 – a 20.5% rise – with claims-related failures accounting for 59% of that total. The obligation to update policyholders at least every 20 business days was breached 18,350 times, up 67% on the year before.
For brokers, those failures translate directly into client calls and complaint management. Technology that creates an objective, timestamped record of vehicle condition from lodgement – and feeds it into a live reporting system – addresses a specific part of that chain.
RAVIN AI, co-founded by Eliron Ekstein, develops vehicle inspection systems built on deep learning and computer-vision models and serves clients across the insurance, fleet management, rental, and retail automotive sectors internationally.
The company already has an Australian presence. In October 2025, IAG’s digital motor insurance brand ROLLiN’ announced it had integrated RAVIN AI’s technology into its claims workflow, reporting that early usage had cut average claim cycle times by 50%. That figure is self-reported from ROLLiN’s own early-stage data, but it gives brokers a local reference point for the technology’s application in a comparable market.
Ekstein said the Clarion integration extends that reach to a different part of the Australian market. “Clarion Claims is changing how motor claims are handled in Australia by putting transparency and speed first. Embedding RAVIN’s computer-vision model in Clarion’s workflows makes accurate, automated damage analysis available from any mobile device, helping Australian insurers, brokers, MGAs, and fleet teams resolve claims faster,” he said.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) named insurance complaints and claims handling as one of its enforcement priorities for 2026. The General Insurance Code of Practice is under concurrent redraft – public consultation closed in July 2026 – with proposed changes including, for the first time, legally enforceable insurer commitments.
For brokers assessing which claims partners to work with, that regulatory direction adds weight to tools that produce auditable records and automated communication from lodgement.
The integration is live. Further information is available at clarionclaims.com.au and ravin.ai.
